chains_identified.name: Null-Origin CORS + Sandboxed Iframe → Full Credentialed API Exfiltration (No XSS Required)
steps: Host attacker page on any domain (no XSS required — null-origin path)
Attacker page creates sandboxed iframe with srcdoc attribute containing fetch() calls to backend
Browser sends Origin: null for requests from sandboxed iframe
Backend reflects 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: null' + 'Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true'
Fetch requests carry victim's session cookies (credentials:include) — CORS allows them
Attacker reads /auth/me → get user identity + JWT token
Enumerate /rbac/me/permissions → get full permission set
Exfiltrate /users, /accounts, /contacts, /deals, /connect-points — full CRM data
Use non-HttpOnly csrf-token cookie (readable via CORS GET) to forge POST/PUT/PATCH requests
Full read/write access to all backend API routes as the victim
missing_evidence: Live PoC confirming null-origin sandboxed iframe carries victim cookies in cross-origin fetch
Confirmation that victim session cookies are SameSite=None or SameSite=Lax (required for cross-site CORS delivery)
Evidence that /auth/me returns user data when called with valid session cookie via CORS

chains_identified.name: Azure AD OIDC Nonce Absent → id_token Replay → Account Takeover
steps: Initiate Azure AD OAuth2 OIDC flow via /api/auth/signin/azure-ad
Complete authentication with attacker-controlled Azure AD account in same tenant
Capture id_token JWT from Azure AD (attacker owns this token legitimately)
Modify 'sub', 'email', and 'preferred_username' claims in id_token payload
Re-sign JWT if NEXTAUTH_SECRET is weak or reuse unsigned token if nonce not validated
If nonce claim is absent in id_token verification — submit modified id_token to /api/auth/callback/azure-ad
NextAuth creates session for the victim user whose email was substituted
Full account takeover — attacker is now authenticated as victim user
missing_evidence: Active Azure AD OAuth flow to confirm nonce parameter is absent from authorization request
Capture and decode id_token to confirm nonce claim is missing from token
Test if NextAuth /api/auth/callback/azure-ad validates nonce before creating session
Determine NEXTAUTH_SECRET length/entropy — weak secret enables JWT forgery
Confirm whether Azure AD tenant is single-org or multi-tenant (multi-tenant widens attacker surface)

chains_identified.name: Authenticated User → IDOR on /rbac/users/{id}/role → Self-Escalation to Admin
steps: Authenticate as any low-privilege user (required: valid Azure AD account in tenant)
GET /rbac/roles → enumerate available role IDs (roles list endpoint confirmed to exist)
GET /rbac/me/permissions → confirm current user's role and permission scope
PUT /rbac/users/{own_user_id}/role with body {role_id: <admin_role_id>}
If server does not check that requesting user cannot modify own role → privilege escalation
Alternatively: GET /rbac/roles/user-assignments → discover other user IDs
PUT /rbac/users/{other_user_id}/role with admin role ID → escalate another account
Result: admin access to full CRM, user management, org settings, billing
missing_evidence: Authenticated session token (any valid user) to test RBAC endpoints
Confirmed role IDs from GET /rbac/roles response
Server response to PUT /rbac/users/{self_id}/role with admin role ID
Confirmation that /users/{id}/access PATCH is also missing server-side auth checks

chains_identified.name: Authenticated → GraphQL Introspection → Schema Discovery → Privileged Mutation
steps: Obtain any authenticated session (required: valid Azure AD account)
POST /graphql with introspection query: {__schema{types{name,fields{name,type{name}}}}}
Map full GraphQL schema — identify all queries and mutations
Identify high-value mutations: role assignment, user deletion, org config, billing ops
Attempt mutations with own session — check if authorization is enforced per-mutation
If GraphQL lacks field-level authorization → execute privileged mutations as low-privilege user
Escalate to admin or exfiltrate data not accessible via REST API layer
missing_evidence: Authenticated session token to reach /graphql endpoint (auth-gated)
Introspection query response (schema currently unknown)
Presence of mutations in schema (could be query-only GraphQL)
Field-level authorization bypass evidence — introspection enabled does not confirm authz bypass

chains_identified.name: Azure Container Apps → IMDS Metadata Token → Azure AD Lateral Movement
steps: Confirm Azure Container App has system-assigned or user-assigned managed identity
From inside container context (via SSRF or RCE) — probe http://169.254.169.254/metadata/instance
GET http://169.254.169.254/metadata/identity/oauth2/token?api-version=2018-02-01&resource=https://graph.microsoft.com/
IMDS returns managed identity access token for Microsoft Graph API
Use token to enumerate Azure AD users, groups, app registrations, service principals
Identify Azure Key Vault, Storage, or other resources accessible to managed identity
Exfiltrate secrets from Key Vault or access production databases/storage
Alternatively: use managed identity token to forge new Azure AD app credentials for persistent access
missing_evidence: SSRF vector into container network or RCE on container to reach IMDS
Confirmation that managed identity is assigned to the Container App
IMDS endpoint response (169.254.169.254 accessible from container network only)
Azure Key Vault or storage resources associated with managed identity
